title: BootRecord
description: Everything kokuin knows about one boot. This is the root of the JSON format.

boot.description: Which boot this is, and on what system.

events.description: Everything that happened, in the best-known chronological order.

milestones.description: Key moments of the boot, in chronological order.

processes.description: Processes that ran during the boot, sorted by start time.

schema_version.description:
Version of the format, as `MAJOR.MINOR`. A new minor version only adds optional
fields and enum values; a new major version may break consumers.

sources.description: What happened with each data source: what could be read, and why not.

stages.description:
Time span of each boot phase, in boot order. Phases that did not happen are
absent.

BootInfo.description: Which boot this record describes, and on what system.

boot_id.description:
Random identifier the kernel gives to each boot
(`/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`).

bootloader.description: The bootloader that started the kernel, when it could be identified.

init.description: The init system (PID 1), when it could be identified.

started_at.description: Wall-clock time of the kernel start (boot clock `0`), in RFC 3339 format.

captured_at.description: Wall-clock time when the record was written, in RFC 3339 format.

tool.description: Name of the program that made the record (`kokuin-cli`).

CaptureMethod.description: How the data of a record was collected.

oneOf.description:
Reconstructed after the boot from what the system still remembers (logs,
firmware tables, running processes). Processes that already exited are missing.
Recorded live during the boot by `kokuin-init`.
Recorded live with the extra kernel tracing of deep mode.
A value from a newer schema version. Never produced by this version.

ComponentInfo.description: A software component of the boot chain (bootloader, init system).

explain_id.description: Identifier of the explanation of this component in the knowledge base.

id.description:
Stable lowercase identifier (for example `grub`, `systemd-boot`, `runit`,
`systemd`, `openrc`). The known identifiers are listed in `docs/format.md`.

Confidence.description: How much a time (or a time span) can be trusted.

oneOf.description:
Read from a clock by the component itself (kernel log timestamp, process event,
firmware performance record).

Derived from a clock, with a known imprecision: for example a firmware time
converted to the boot clock, or a process start time with a resolution of one
clock tick.

No clock at all: the position was deduced from the order of events (for example
a TPM measurement placed between two timed events).

DmiInfo.description: Hardware identification from the SMBIOS/DMI tables (`/sys/class/dmi/id`).

oneOf.description: The session became ready and the settle time elapsed.
The maximum recording time elapsed before the session was ready.
The user stopped the recording.
A post-hoc capture: the data is a snapshot taken at `captured_at`.
A value from a newer schema version. Never produced by this version.

Event.description:
One thing that happened during the boot.

In a record, events are sorted in the best-known chronological order, including
events without a time.

confidence.description: How much `t_ns` and `dur_ns` can be trusted.

data.description:
Source-specific details. The keys used by each source are listed in
`docs/format.md`.

dur_ns.description: How long it lasted, in ns, for events that have a duration.

explain_id.description: Identifier of the explanation of this event in the knowledge base.

message.description: The original message, as written by the component, when there is one.

process.description: The process this event is about or comes from.

source.description:
Identifier of the data source that produced this event: the `id` of one of the
record `sources`.

stage.description: The boot phase this event is attributed to.

t_ns.description:
When it happened on the boot clock, in ns. Absent when no clock was available
(the position in the event list still gives the order).

EventId.description: Identifier of an [`Event`], unique within one record.

oneOf.description: A log message (kernel log, init system log...).
A timestamp reported by the firmware (ACPI FPDT).

Something the firmware or bootloader measured into the TPM before running or
using it (measured boot).
A firmware setting or EFI variable (boot order, Secure Boot state...).
A kernel initialization function (initcall), with its duration when known.
A process started (exec).
A process exited.
A service changed state (`data.state` holds the new state).
A filesystem was mounted.
A device was detected, or a driver bound to it.
A value from a newer schema version. Never produced by this version.

FirmwareKind.description: Kind of firmware that booted the machine.

oneOf.description: UEFI firmware.
Legacy PC BIOS (or UEFI in legacy/CSM mode).
Something else (device tree based boards...), or not detected.

LogLevel.description: Severity of a log message, as defined by syslog.

oneOf.description: The system is unusable.
Action must be taken immediately.
Critical condition.
Error.
Warning.
Normal but significant condition.
Informational.
Debug message.

dmi.description: Hardware identification from the SMBIOS/DMI tables.

firmware.description: Kind of firmware that booted the machine.

uefi.description: UEFI details, when the firmware is UEFI.

Milestone.description: A key moment of the boot, placed on the boot clock.

event.description: The event this milestone was detected from, if any.

explain_id.description: Identifier of the explanation of this milestone in the knowledge base.

t_ns.description: When it happened on the boot clock, in ns.

MilestoneKind.description:
A key moment of the boot, in boot order. Each kind appears at most once in a
record.

oneOf.description: The firmware starts running, right after the CPU leaves reset (FPDT `ResetEnd`).
The firmware starts loading the bootloader image (FPDT `OsLoaderLoadImageStart`).
The firmware starts executing the bootloader (FPDT `OsLoaderStartImageStart`).
The firmware hands the machine over to the OS (end of UEFI `ExitBootServices`).
The Linux kernel starts. Always at `0` on the boot clock.
The kernel runs the initramfs `/init`.
The real root filesystem is mounted.
The init system of the real root filesystem starts as PID 1.
The init system starts launching services.
A graphics driver is ready to display something (DRM/KMS driver initialized).
The display manager (login screen) starts.
The user session starts (login done, or automatic login).
The compositor (or X server) of the user session starts.
The desktop is usable: the session is up and the system has settled.
The recording stopped.
A value from a newer schema version. Never produced by this version.

Process.description:
A process that ran during the boot, from its creation (`fork`) to its exit.

A process can replace its program (`exec`) several times during its life:
`comm`, `cmdline` and `exe` describe the last program it ran, and each `exec` is
also an event of kind `process_start`.

cmdline.description: Full command line of the last program. Empty when unknown, and for kernel threads.

comm.description:
Short command name of the last program, as the kernel knows it (at most 15
characters).

confidence.description: How much `start_ns` and `end_ns` can be trusted.

end_ns.description:
When the process exited on the boot clock, in ns. Absent if it was still
running at the end of the capture.

exe.description: Path of the executable of the last program.

exit_code.description: Exit code, if the process exited normally.

exit_signal.description: Number of the signal that killed the process, if a signal killed it.

explain_id.description: Identifier of the explanation of this program in the knowledge base.

parent.description: The process that started this one.

ppid.description: PID of the parent, also given when the parent itself is not in the record.

service.description: Name of the service this process belongs to, when the init system tells it.

stage.description: The boot phase this process is attributed to.

start_ns.description: When the process was created on the boot clock, in ns.

uid.description:
User id the process ran as. Processes of normal users (1000 and above) belong
to a user session.

ProcessId.description:
Identifier of a [`Process`], unique within one record.

Different from the PID: the kernel reuses PIDs, so one PID can belong to several
processes during a boot.

SourceReport.description: What happened with one data source during the capture.

explain_id.description: Identifier of the explanation of this source in the knowledge base.

id.description:
Identifier of the source (for example `fpdt`, `tpm_eventlog`, `kmsg`). Events
reference it in their `source` field. The known identifiers are listed in
`docs/format.md`.

raw_files.description:
Raw files saved from this source, relative to the record directory. They keep
the original data so a record can be analyzed again with better rules.

status.description: Whether the source could be read.

SourceStatus.description: Whether a data source could be read.

oneOf.description: Fully read.
Read, but some data is missing (`reason` says what and why).

Not present on this system (`reason` says why: no TPM, BIOS boot, missing
kernel option, not running as root...).
Present but reading it failed (`reason` holds the error).
A value from a newer schema version. Never produced by this version.

Stage.description:
A phase of the boot, in the order in which phases start.

Phases can overlap: services keep starting while the graphical session comes up,
and the kernel keeps logging after it started the init system.

oneOf.description: From power-on to the firmware starting the bootloader (UEFI or BIOS).
The bootloader (GRUB, systemd-boot...) choosing and loading the kernel.
The kernel initializing the hardware and itself, until it runs the first process.

The early userspace from the initramfs, until it switches to the real root
filesystem. Absent when the system boots without an initramfs.
The init system (PID 1) setting up the base system: mounts, devices, hostname...
Services being started by the init system or its service supervisor.
Display stack coming up: graphics driver, display manager or compositor.
The user session starting, until the desktop is ready and the system settled.
Everything after the session is ready.
A value from a newer schema version. Never produced by this version.

StageSpan.description: The time span of one [`Stage`] during this boot.

confidence.description: How much `start_ns` and `end_ns` can be trusted.

end_ns.description:
End of the stage on the boot clock, in ns. Absent if the stage did not end
before the capture.

explain_id.description: Identifier of the explanation of this stage in the knowledge base.

start_ns.description: Start of the stage on the boot clock, in ns.

platform_bits.description: Bitness of the firmware (32 or 64), which can differ from the kernel's.

spec_version.description: UEFI specification version the firmware implements (for example `2.70`).
